decision: Where do intervals come from for the Forecast page?
options: (a) SQL table forecast_substrateBE_hdd_region already has Forecast-Lower/Upper or quantile ValueType rows -> just unfilter ingestion+transform; (b) upstream system must add them; (c) compute in this pipeline via residual bootstrap on backtest; (d) quantile models
recommended_default: (a) FIRST verify the DB: run SELECT DISTINCT [ValueType] on the source table. If Lower/Upper exist, that is by far the safest path.
Both (80 inner band + 95 outer band) if available; otherwise 95 only

options: model_native probabilistic / residual_bootstrap / empirical_backtest residual bands / quantile model
recommended_default: model_native if the DB provides them; else empirical_backtest residual bands calibrated on the frozen backtest (governed, documented)
Asymmetric (true quantiles) when available; symmetric only as a documented fallback

options: per model / per key / per horizon / global
recommended_default: Per key x model x horizon (uncertainty grows with horizon)
Yes if method is residual/empirical, so coverage is honest

decision: Cap bounds at zero if value cannot be negative?
recommended_default: Yes for non-negative resources (cap lower at 0), applied at generation, not in Shiny
Governed if model_native from the DB; diagnostic (clearly labeled) if pipeline-derived

decision: How to label in the Forecast Chart?
recommended_default: 'Prediction interval (95%)' with method + source in Data notes

decision: What if a key/model has no intervals?
options: hide band / show point-only with note
recommended_default: Show point forecast only with a clear 'No prediction interval available' note
